text: In the eleventh year, on the first day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me:
Son of man, because Tyre said of Jerusalem, "Aha! The gateway of the peoples is shattered; it has swung open to me. Now that she lies in ruins, I will be filled,"
therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: I am against you, Tyre. I will raise many nations against you, as the sea raises its waves.
They will destroy the walls of Tyre and tear down her towers. I will scrape away her rubble and leave her a bare rock.
Out in the sea she will become a place for spreading nets, for I have spoken, declares the Lord GOD. She will become plunder for the nations,
and her daughter villages on the mainland will be put to the sword. Then they will know that I am the LORD.
For this is what the Lord GOD says: I am bringing against Tyre from the north Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, king of kings, with horses and chariots, with horsemen and a vast army.
He will put your daughter villages on the mainland to the sword. He will set up siegeworks against you, raise a ramp against you, and lift his shields against you.
He will drive his battering rams against your walls and break down your towers with his iron tools.

versions.text: He will drive his battering rams against your walls and break down your towers with his weapons.
versions.explanation: חַרְבוֹת here denotes demolition implements (axes/crowbars) rather than "weapons" in general; a sword would not break down a tower, so a more concrete rendering is clearer.

text: His horses will be so many that their dust will cover you. Your walls will shake at the noise of horsemen, wheels, and chariots when he enters your gates as men enter a city whose walls are breached.

versions.text: His horses will be so many that their dust will cover you. Your walls will shake at the noise of cavalry, wagons, and chariots when he enters your gates as men enter a city whose walls are breached.
versions.explanation: גַּלְגַּל means "wheel" (the rumbling of chariot wheels), not "wagon"; the triad horseman–wheel–chariot is also more vivid for oral reading. Note the suggested text keeps the first sentence unchanged.

text: With the hooves of his horses he will trample all your streets. He will kill your people with the sword, and your mighty pillars will topple to the ground.
They will plunder your wealth and loot your merchandise. They will break down your walls and demolish your fine houses, and they will throw your stones, your timber, and your rubble into the water.
I will silence the noise of your songs, and the music of your harps will be heard no more.
I will make you a bare rock; you will become a place for spreading nets. You will never be rebuilt, for I the LORD have spoken, declares the Lord GOD.
This is what the Lord GOD says to Tyre: Will not the coastlands quake at the sound of your fall, when the wounded groan and the slaughter rages within you?

Then all the princes of the sea will step down from their thrones, lay aside their robes, and strip off their embroidered garments. Clothed in terror, they will sit on the ground, trembling every moment, appalled at you.
They will raise this lament over you: "How you have perished, city of renown, peopled by seafarers! You and your citizens were a power on the sea, spreading your terror over all who lived there.
Now the coastlands tremble on the day of your fall; the islands of the sea are terrified at your passing."
For this is what the Lord GOD says: When I make you a desolate city, like cities no longer inhabited, when I bring the deep up over you and the vast waters cover you,

then I will bring you down with those who go down to the pit, to the people of long ago. I will make you dwell in the earth below, among ancient ruins, with those who go down to the pit, so that you will not return or take your place in the land of the living.[^1]

versions.text: then I will bring you down with those who go down to the pit, to the people of long ago. I will make you dwell in the earth below, among ancient ruins, with those who go down to the pit, so that you will not return or take your place in the land of the living.
versions.explanation: The final clause of the Hebrew text is textually and syntactically difficult; the rendering follows an interpretive reading, so a brief footnote would help the reader without altering the flow of the text.

versions.text:
so that you will not return or take your place in the land of the living.[^1]

[^1]: The Hebrew of this last clause is difficult; it may also be read, "and I will set glory in the land of the living."
versions.explanation: The current verse has lost the greater part of the Hebrew. Missing are וְהוֹרַדְתִּיךְ אֶת־יוֹרְדֵי בוֹר אֶל־עַם עוֹלָם ("then I will bring you down with those who go down to the pit, to the people of long ago") and וְהוֹשַׁבְתִּיךְ בְּאֶרֶץ תַּחְתִּיּוֹת כָּחֳרָבוֹת מֵעוֹלָם אֶת־יוֹרְדֵי בוֹר ("I will make you dwell in the earth below, among ancient ruins, with those who go down to the pit"). Only the final clause survives, leaving the verse without a main clause and breaking the connection with verse 19. The wording is restored from the earlier revision; the existing footnote on the difficult final clause is retained.

text: I will bring you to a horrible end, and you will be no more. You will be sought, but you will never be found again, declares the Lord GOD.
